title: 2006 AMC 12A Problem 18
statement: The function \(f\) has the property that for each real number \(x\) in its domain, \(\frac{1}{x}\) is also in its domain and \[ f(x) + f\!\left(\frac{1}{x}\right) = x. \] What is the largest set of real numbers that can be in the domain of \(f?\)

solutions.text:
Replacing \(x\) by \(\frac{1}{x}\) gives \(f\!\left(\tfrac{1}{x}\right) + f(x) = \tfrac{1}{x}.\) Together with \(f(x) + f\!\left(\tfrac{1}{x}\right) = x,\) this requires \(x = \tfrac{1}{x},\) so \(x = \pm 1.\)

Both values are consistent, with \(f(1) = \tfrac{1}{2}\) and \(f(-1) = -\tfrac{1}{2}.\) So the largest possible domain is \(\{-1, 1\}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Substitute \(\frac{1}{x}\) in place of \(x\) to get a second equation
